main_text.p: tentia in Assertion. Teuton . art. 21. Qui semel mentitur, hic certissime ex Deo non est, & suspectus in omnibus habetur, quantus mendax habendus erit Hottingerus, ex hoc sui Lutheri placito, qui non semel, sed bis, terque, quaterque, imo semper mendax deprehensus est? Et quidem, si

p.i: Quo semel est imbuta recens seruabit odorem,

main_text.p: Quanto magis diutissime mendacis imbutus foedissimis Hottingerus, Cacabus, mendaciorum seruabit foetorem. Etenim nihil aliud Arabibus denotat الطبخه [?] Hottinger, quam Cacabus, Olla. Unde egregie Poëta Arab de Hominum cogno-mine,

وقل ما ابصرت عيناك من رجل
إلا ومعناه ان قشت في لقمه [?]

p.i: Pauci sunt, quos tui vident oculi, homines,
Quorum notionem, si perquisieris, non designat cognomen.

main_text.p: Afferit itaque الطبخه [?] Hottinger, Pa-trum mentionem, & allegata obvia esse apud Orientales, non haberi tamen ab eis, vt Cynosuram, & Canonem; Sed habentur; ergo mentitur, & ex illo foetidissimo Cacabo, hoc

page.notes: The Arabic verse lines and the inline Arabic word "الطبخه" are read from a small, slightly blurred print. Uncertain letters and the final words of the second verse line are marked [?]. The Arabic word after "Hottinger" is also doubtful. Hyphenation "Pa-trum" and "cogno-mine" follows the printed line ends. Long s is normalised to s, and u/v and i/j are normalised as the rules require. The page has no margin notes and no running head.
